Antipsychotic adjuncts to clozapine: meta-analysis results

21 October 2026

1 Summary

The review includes 16 randomised placebo-controlled trials that added an antipsychotic to clozapine; 14 of them (847 participants randomised) report numbers that can be pooled. Pooled with a random-effects model, the adjuncts did not improve total symptoms significantly (14 trials, g = −0.19, 95% CI −0.40 to 0.03, p = 0.092; I² = 53%). Positive symptoms (13 trials, g = −0.10, 95% CI −0.44 to 0.24, p = 0.573) and negative symptoms (14 trials, g = −0.11, 95% CI −0.31 to 0.08, p = 0.255) showed no significant effect either.

In the sensitivity analyses, the 8 schizophrenia-only trials gave g = −0.37, 95% CI −0.60 to −0.14, p = 0.002, and the 10 trials reporting endpoint scores gave g = −0.21, 95% CI −0.51 to 0.08, p = 0.159.

Effect sizes are Hedges’ g, adjunct minus placebo, so a negative g favours the adjunct. Models are random effects with a REML estimate of τ² and z-based tests.

3.3 Certainty of the evidence (GRADE)

The GRADE judgements are proposals from GRADE.csv for the review team to confirm.

Table 3. Summary of findings
Outcome Trials (participants) Hedges’ g (95% CI) I² 95% prediction interval Certainty (GRADE) Reasons for rating down
Total symptoms 14 (805) −0.19 (−0.40 to 0.03) 53% −0.80 to 0.42 Very low Risk of bias (−1): Nine of the 14 trials, carrying 61% of the weight, were rated some concerns (none high), and the five low-risk trials together showed no effect. Inconsistency (−1): I² was 53% and the 95% prediction interval ran from a moderate benefit to a small harm. Imprecision (−1): The 95% CI includes both no effect and a small benefit (g of 0.2 or more in favour of the adjunct).
Positive symptoms 13 (748) −0.10 (−0.44 to 0.24) 80% −1.23 to 1.03 Very low Risk of bias (−1): Trials rated some concerns carried 68% of the weight. Inconsistency (−2): I² was 80% and the 95% prediction interval ran from a large benefit to a large harm; four different positive-symptom scales were used. Imprecision (−1): The 95% CI includes both no effect and a small benefit.
Negative symptoms 14 (805) −0.11 (−0.31 to 0.08) 43% −0.62 to 0.39 Very low Risk of bias (−1): Trials rated some concerns carried 61% of the weight. Inconsistency (−1): I² was 43%, but the 95% prediction interval ran from a moderate benefit to a small harm. Imprecision (−1): The 95% CI includes both no effect and a small benefit.
